items.note: Billy's recipe is written for 12–14 lb. This size feeds 10 with leftovers. If frozen, start thawing 4 days ahead.

items.text: Order the turkey, 15–16 lb
items.note: Fresh from a butcher, or a store pre-order.

items.text: Test-fit the oven
items.note: Roasting pan on the bottom rack with a second rack above it. Check that a 13×9 dish and two sheet pans fit. This decides how much can share the oven with the turkey.

items.text: Bake a test batch of the rolls (optional)
items.note: One batch makes 14–16. Freeze a few to try the freezer route.

items.text: Plan fridge space
items.note: A 15–16 lb turkey needs a full shelf, plus room for stuffing, yams and rolls.

items.text: Buy pantry items and equipment
items.note: Flour, sugars, yeast, stock, spices, foil, parchment, twine.

items.text: Buy the bread loaf for stuffing
Charge the Bluetooth thermometer and check the probe
Frozen turkey only: move it to the fridge
items.note: Allow 24 hours per 5 lb, so about 3 days for 15–16 lb. Keep it on a tray on the bottom shelf.

items.text: Buy produce, butter, milk and eggs
Buy fresh herbs
Pick up the fresh turkey
Make the cranberry sauce
items.note: Boil 1 cup water with 1¼ cups sugar, add the cranberries, return to a boil, then cover and simmer about 15 minutes until very thick. Off the heat, stir in cinnamon, nutmeg and orange zest and press the berries to break them up. Use a high-sided pot (they splatter). Keeps 7 days in the fridge.

items.text: Dry the bread cubes
items.note: 300°F for 25–30 minutes until firm. Cool, then store airtight.

items.text: Make and bake the rolls, two separate batches
items.note: Dough rises 1–2 hours, shaped rolls about 1 hour, then 20–25 minutes at 350°F on a lower rack. Cover tightly. They keep 2–3 days at room temperature. Reheat covered at 300°F for about 10 minutes.

items.text: Simmer the neck and giblets for the gravy
items.note: From the turkey cavity. Bring to a boil in water, simmer about 1 hour. Keep the liquid. Pick the neck meat, dice it with the heart and gizzard (discard the liver), and refrigerate both.

items.text: Prep vegetables
items.note: Peel and trim the carrots (leave them whole). Chop onions and celery for the stuffing.

items.text: Make the vinaigrette and toast the pecans
items.note: Shake in a jar: ½ cup olive oil, ¼ cup apple cider vinegar, 1 tbsp Dijon, 1 tbsp maple syrup, 1 minced small shallot, ½ tsp salt, pepper. Refrigerate. Toast the pecans in a dry skillet over medium heat for 4–5 minutes, stirring, then cool and store airtight.

items.text: Trim and blanch the green beans
items.note: Boil in well-salted water for 2–3 minutes, then plunge into ice water. Dry well and refrigerate in a towel-lined container.

items.text: Lay out dishes, pans, serving bowls and utensils
Set the table
Stuffing: brown the sausage, sauté the vegetables, mix with bread, herbs, stock and eggs
items.note: Add the stock slowly. Stop when the bread is moist but not soggy.

items.text: Stuffing into the oven at 350°F
items.note: Covered for 25 minutes, then uncovered for about 20.

items.text: Yams into the oven
items.note: Shortcut from Billy's page: slice, boil 4–6 minutes, drain, coat in the butter and sugar mix, bake at 375°F for 25–30 minutes. Check they are tender.

items.text: Roast the whole carrots at 425°F
items.note: Toss with 3 tbsp olive oil, 1 tsp salt and pepper. One layer on a parchment-lined sheet pan with space between them. 25–30 minutes, turning once, until browned and just tender with a little bite left. They finish cooking in the reheat.

items.text: Cool the stuffing, yams and carrots for 30 minutes, cover, and move to the fridge
items.note: They are reheated from cold later.

items.text: Whip the herb butter
items.note: 5–7 minutes in the stand mixer, then mix in herbs, garlic, salt and pepper.

items.text: Prep the turkey
items.note: Pat dry. Stuff the cavity with lemon, parsley and bay leaves. Butter under the skin on the breast and back. Truss.

items.text: Oven to 450°F
Turkey in: bottom rack, breast up, 450°F for 22–25 minutes
items.note: Until browned on top.

items.text: Flip the turkey breast down, cover the top with bacon, oven to 350°F
items.note: Very hot. Gloves, towels and a second person.

items.text: Remove the bacon and return the turkey to the oven
Start watching the thermometer
items.note: 9–11 minutes per lb after the flip puts the finish at roughly 3:55–4:35. Pull at 165°F in the thickest part.

items.text: Turkey out. Rest on the board, loosely covered in foil
items.note: Billy rests it 15–20 minutes. Wrapped fully in foil or in a cooler it holds up to 90 minutes.

items.text: Reheat stuffing (splash of stock) and yams, covered, at 350°F for about 20 minutes. Glaze the carrots and put them in uncovered
items.note: Carrot glaze: melt 2 tbsp butter with 2 tbsp honey and 1 tbsp chopped thyme, toss with the carrots on their pan. Short on oven room? Warm them in the air fryer at 350°F for 6–8 minutes instead.

items.text: Gravy: pour the pan drippings into the fat separator and skim most of the fat
items.note: Whisk 1 cup drippings with ½ cup flour over medium heat until golden. Add 4 cups stock and 1 more cup drippings, whisk 5–8 minutes until thick, then stir in the giblets. Thin with giblet liquid. Taste before salting, since the bacon makes the drippings salty. Keep warm on low.

items.text: Potatoes: boil 10 minutes, drain, air-dry 10 minutes, shake at the 5-minute mark
Casseroles out, keep covered. Oven to 450°F (475°F without fan)
Potatoes on two sheet pans with oil and spices, into the oven
items.note: Space them an inch apart. 20 minutes, flip, 20 more.

items.text: Carve the turkey
items.note: A job for your helper.

items.text: Flip the potatoes
Sauté the green beans in two batches
items.note: Large skillet, medium-high, 1 tbsp oil and 1 tbsp butter per batch, 4–5 minutes. Add half the sliced garlic for the last minute. Finish with lemon zest, a squeeze of juice, salt and pepper.

items.text: Warm the rolls
items.note: Air fryer on low for a few minutes, checking often.

items.text: Assemble the spinach salad
items.note: Take the vinaigrette out of the fridge at 5:00 and shake it. Slice the pears now, not earlier, so they don't brown. Toss the spinach with about two-thirds of the dressing, then top with pears, pomegranate, pecans and shaved Parmesan. Extra dressing on the side. A good job for a helper.

items.text: Potatoes out, drizzle with melted butter
Gravy, cranberry sauce and everything to the table
Sit down

lines.text: Simmer the neck and giblets the day before. Short on drippings? Top up with 1–2 tbsp butter and a little stock.

lines.label: Ingredients
lines.text: 2 tbsp olive oil, 2 tbsp butter, 4 garlic cloves thinly sliced, zest and juice of 1 lemon, salt and pepper

lines.label: Method
lines.text: Blanch 2–3 min the day before, then sauté in two batches for 4–5 min just before serving. Garlic goes in for the last minute so it does not burn.

lines.label: Size
lines.text: 3 lb medium carrots (about 20) for 10

lines.label: Ingredients
lines.text: 3 tbsp olive oil, 1 tsp salt, pepper. Glaze: 2 tbsp butter, 2 tbsp honey, 1 tbsp chopped fresh thyme.

lines.label: Method
lines.text: Roast whole at 425°F for 25–30 min at midday, chill, then glaze and reheat uncovered at 350°F for about 20 min with the casseroles.

lines.label: Size
lines.text: One batch (recipe serves 10)

lines.label: Method
lines.text: Simmer cranberries with sugar and water about 15 min, finish with orange zest, cinnamon and nutmeg. Chill 30–45 min.

lines.label: Make ahead
lines.text: Up to 2 days ahead (keeps 7 days in the fridge, or freezes for 3 months).

menu.name: Spinach salad with pears and pecans

lines.label: Size
lines.text: 15 oz baby spinach for 10

lines.label: Ingredients
lines.text: 2 ripe pears, 1 cup pomegranate seeds, 1 cup toasted pecans, 3 oz shaved Parmesan

lines.label: Dressing
lines.text: Apple cider vinaigrette: ½ cup olive oil, ¼ cup cider vinegar, 1 tbsp each Dijon and maple syrup, 1 small shallot, salt and pepper

lines.label: Make ahead
lines.text: Dressing and pecans the day before. No cooking on the day, just slice the pears and toss at 5:45.

callouts.title: If the turkey is late.
callouts.text: Leave it in until it reads 165°F. Skip the oven reheat, warm the stuffing, yams and carrots in the microwave in portions, and put the potatoes in once the turkey is out.

callouts.title: For a lighter day.
callouts.text: Bake the stuffing, yams and carrots on D−1 and reheat them from the fridge on the day.
